The white fluffy, feathery mycelium growing on a brown/tan tomato stem is highly characteristic of **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (caused by *Sclerotinia sclerotiorum*). This fungus produces dense white cottony mycelium on infected stems, often with embedded sclerotia. The granular texture visible on the stem surface is consistent with this pathogen's sporulation.

The reference image for Sclerotinia shows whole-plant collapse, which is consistent with the stem damage visible here — the stem canker/mycelial colonization shown in the test image would ultimately cause wilting and collapse. Gray Mold (Botrytis) is a close alternative, but the white (not gray) color and feathery radiating pattern is more consistent with Sclerotinia.
